title: Bechamel Sauce
subtitle: classic white sauce -- the foundation of lasagne, cauliflower cheese, and more
excerpt: Bechamel is one of the simplest and most used sauces in European cooking. It is made from equal quantities of butter and flour cooked together, then milk added gradually until the sauce is smooth and thick. It is the base for cauliflower cheese, lasagne, and moussaka.
sourceNotes: One of the five French mother sauces. Named after the Marquis de Bechamel, a French courtier, though the sauce existed before him. It is the foundation of many European dishes from lasagne to croque monsieur.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat gently and whisk to smooth any lumps.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Useful to have in the freezer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in the fridge for 3 days. Press cling film directly onto the surface to prevent a skin forming.

content.text: Add the milk gradually and whisk thoroughly between each addition. This is what prevents lumps. Warm milk will incorporate more smoothly than cold.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour all at once.
Stir constantly for 2 minutes to cook the flour. The mixture should look like wet sand and smell faintly biscuity.
Add the milk in a thin stream, whisking constantly. Add only a little at a time and wait for each addition to be fully incorporated before adding more.
Continue whisking over medium heat until the sauce is thick and smooth. This takes about 8 minutes.
Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Use immediately or press cling film onto the surface to cool.

items.cause: Milk added too fast or roux unevenly cooked
items.fix: Pass through a fine sieve and whisk vigorously. For large lumps, blend briefly.
Cook the butter and flour together for a full 2 minutes before adding any milk.
Whisk in more warm milk until the correct consistency.

content.text: Bechamel is one of the five classical French mother sauces and appears in the cooking of Italy, Greece, and much of northern Europe. In Italy it is known as besciamella and is used in lasagne and baked pasta dishes. In Greece it tops moussaka. In Britain it is used in cauliflower cheese and fish pie. It is one of the most useful things you can learn to make.
